extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners/applicants seeking procedural guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, formatting, and handling Office actions and for petitions to make applications "special" (including accelerated examination and other grounds for advancement). Covers examiner conduct, mailing/filing procedures, and the criteria/requirements for various petitions to advance examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Summary Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each action should include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination. Form PTO-326 "Office Action Summary" should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PTO-326 to make the status of claims easily traceable; include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Claims Retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and claims retained under 37 CFR 1.146 should be treated as set out in MPEP § 821 to § 821.04(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the MPEP sections referenced for handling retained claims; consult MPEP § 821 et seq. for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims in Losing Party of Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for treatment of claims in the application of the losing party in interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter 2300 when dealing with claims of the losing party in interference proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index of Claims should be kept up to date as set forth in MPEP § 719.04. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Index of Claims is current per MPEP § 719.04; follow IFW Manual for image file wrapper handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting Claims for Pro Se (Inventor-Filed) Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When, during the examination of a pro se application it becomes apparent to the examiner that there is patentable subject matter disclosed in the application, the examiner should draft one or more claims for the applicant and indicate in his or her action that such claims would be allowed if incorporated in the application by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice expedites prosecution and aids individual inventors not represented by counsel; it should be applied when it is apparent the applicant is unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Office Actions — Allowable Except As To Form
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application discloses patentable subject matter and it is apparent that the claims are intended to be directed to such subject matter, but claims in present form cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection. The examiner’s action should be constructive in nature and, when possible, should offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete suggestions for correction; note unclaimed aspects or features that if claimed may be favorably considered; suggest interviews when appropriate to accelerate agreement on allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting Unclaimed But Patentable Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied after the search that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates the applicant intends to claim such subject matter, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects or features of the patentable invention have not been claimed and that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Office action to point out potential allowable subject matter that applicant has not claimed; this can guide applicant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent Claims Dependent on Cancelled or Rejected Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is otherwise allowable but is dependent on a canceled claim or on a rejected claim, the Office action should state that the claim would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the allowability contingent on rewriting dependent claims in independent form to include all necessary limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Allowance of Clearly Allowable Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is satisfied that the prior art has been fully developed and some of the claims are clearly allowable, the allowance of such claims should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not delay allowance of claims that are clearly allowable based on developed prior art; process allowance promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph Use — 35 U.S.C. 112, Second Paragraph (¶7.43.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph is to be used when the noted independent claim(s) or the noted dependent claim(s), which depend from an allowable claim, have been rejected solely on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, and would be allowable if amended to overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.43.02 only when dependent claims were rejected solely under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, and would be allowable if amended; follow Examiner Note conditions about applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph — Suggestion of Allowable Drafted Claim(s), Pro Se (¶7.43.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may draft a suggested claim considered to distinguish patentably over the art of record and present it to the applicant for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the suggested claim is not embraced by the original oath or declaration, require a supplemental oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.67; insert complete text of suggested claim(s) in the bracketed area of the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph — Claims Allowed (¶7.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.97 to indicate that Claim [1] is allowed. Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, and 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ standardized form paragraphs to indicate allowance and allowable subject matter as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to Claims — Allowable Subject Matter (¶7.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this objection language to advise applicant how to rewrite dependent claims into allowable independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering Paragraphs in Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the Office action consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number paragraphs consecutively to facilitate identification in future prosecution of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Examples and Test Results
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of the tests and examples should not normally be questioned by the examiner unless there is reasonable basis for questioning the results. If the examiner questions the results, the appropriate claims should be rejected as being based on an insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questioning test/example results, cite 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph; applicant must reply with actual tests or provide relevant arguments; avoid introducing new matter when applicant responds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of 35 U.S.C. 101 for Operability/Utility Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If questions are present as to operability or utility, consideration should be given to the applicability of a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP § 706.03(a) and § 2107 et seq. for guidance when operability or utility concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and Initialing by Preparing Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action will be typed at the end of the action. The telephone number below this should be called if the application is to be discussed or an interview arranged. Form paragraph 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102 should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After typing, the preparing examiner reviews the action for correctness; if not authorized to sign, initial above typed name and forward to authorized signatory examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Inquiry Contact Information (¶7.100-7.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert the name and phone number of the examiner designated to be contacted, days/hours the examiner can normally be reached, and a supervisor contact if attempts to reach the examiner are unsuccessful. Provide PAIR system information for applicant inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate ¶7.100–7.102 form paragraph variant for schedule (non 5/4/9 or 5/4/9 schedule); include PAIR access info and EBC contact details. Fill in bracketed fields per instructions (days, hours, SPE name/number, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing by Authorized Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Although only the original is signed, the word 'Examiner' and the name of the signer should appear on the original and copies. All Office actions and other correspondence should be signed promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely signature by an authorized examiner; include the title and signatory name on original and copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of Action into File Wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: The original, signed by the authorized examiner, is the copy which is placed in the file wrapper. The character of the action, its paper number and the date of mailing are entered in black ink on the outside of the file wrapper under 'Contents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow IFW Manual for image file wrapper processing; ensure proper entry of paper number, action character, and mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing Date and Mailing Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date should not be typed when the Office action is written, but should be stamped or printed on all copies of the action after it has been signed by the authorized signatory examiner and the copies are about to be mailed. Copies are mailed by the Technology Center after the original initialed by the assistant examiner and signed by the authorized signatory examiner has been placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stamp/print mailing date at time of mailing; Technology Center handles mailing after signatures and placement in file; see IFW Manual for IFW processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Returned Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a returned Office action, technical support staff will check whether the Office action was mailed to the correct correspondence address. If not, it should be stamped 'remailed' with the remailing date and mailed to the correct address. The period running against the application begins with the date of remailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correctly addressed but undeliverable and addressed to attorney/agent, a letter with a copy of the Office action may be sent to the first named inventor or assignee informing them. If not deliverable, place the returned action and envelope in the file wrapper; for IFW, add copy of the letter and envelope to IFW. If reply period elapses after remailing with no communication, the application is abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Examination and Docketing Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications are assigned to Technology Centers and are taken up for examination by order of filing date except for those advanced under 37 CFR 1.102. Each examiner will give priority in their docket to the application with the oldest effective U.S. filing date. Reissue applications, reexaminations, and certain special cases receive priority per guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions and priority rules include advancement under 37 CFR 1.102, PCT national stage rules, and Director-determined priorities. Continuation-in-part docketing uses actual filing date; examiner may act using effective filing date if desired. Priority order includes reissue (esp. stayed litigation), ex parte reexamination in litigation, inter partes reexamination in litigation, cases with fixed due dates, and other special categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Timing to Amendments Before Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments before final rejection should be responded to within two months of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely respond to amendments pre-final rejection to avoid delay or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of Special Cases (List of Special Cases (A)-(J))
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated list of special cases that may be advanced out of turn for examination, including (A) inventions of peculiar importance to public service (Director order), (B) petitions making application special, (C) reissues (especially in stayed litigation), (D) applications remanded by appellate tribunal, (E) applications once taken up should be treated as special if transferred, (F) applications appearing to interfere, (G) applications ready for allowance or except for formal matters, (H) applications in condition for final rejection, (I) applications pending more than 5 years, (J) reexamination proceedings involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to diligent prosecution, applications made special often remain special through prosecution including appeals; see MPEP § 708.01 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Make Special — General Requirements and Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special must be supported by a good faith belief that the invention qualifies; petitions filed on or after August 25, 2006 must meet revised accelerated examination program requirements set forth in MPEP § 708.02(a) except for petitions based on applicant’s health or age or under PPH. Applications filed prior to August 25, 2006 follow earlier guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine eligibility based on filing date and petition basis; base statements on good faith per 37 CFR 1.56 and 10.18; noncompliant petitions will be denied or given opportunity to perfect as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Manufacture Grounds (requirements A-D)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special on the ground of prospective manufacture upon filing a petition accompanied by the fee and a statement alleging: (A) possession by prospective manufacturer of sufficient capital and facilities (with approximate amounts/nature) to manufacture in quantity (corroborating statement required if individual), (B) that the prospective manufacturer will not manufacture or increase manufacture unless certain that a patent will be granted, (C) obligation to manufacture in the U.S. upon allowance/issuance to protect investment, (D) that applicant/assignee has made a careful and thorough search of the prior art or has good knowledge of pertinent prior art. Applicant must provide copies of references deemed most closely related if not already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include fee per 37 CFR 1.17(h); provide corroborating evidence for individuals; provide copies of closest references not already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Infringement Grounds (requirements and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special because of actual infringement (not prospective) upon payment of the fee and a statement alleging: (A) an infringing device/product/method actually on the market or in use, (B) a rigid comparison showing some claims are unquestionably infringed, (C) a careful and thorough prior art search or good knowledge of pertinent prior art. Applicant must provide copies of the closest references not already of record. Models/specimens should not be submitted unless requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must demonstrate actual infringement via careful comparison; include closest references; do not submit models/specimens unless asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Applicant’s Health Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon a petition by applicant accompanied by evidence showing applicant's health is such that he or she might not be available to assist in prosecution if it ran its normal course (e.g., doctor's certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal/medical information submitted becomes part of public file if file is public; to avoid public availability, submit information pursuant to MPEP § 724.02; no fee required in the specific regulatory provision referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Applicant’s Age (65+)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon filing a petition including evidence showing the applicant is 65 years of age or more (e.g., applicant’s statement or statement by registered practitioner). No fee is required for such a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal evidence becomes public unless handled under MPEP § 724.02; follow 37 CFR 1.102(c) provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Environmental Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to restoration or maintenance of air, water, and soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must state special status sought due to material environmental enhancement; no fee required. If disclosure does not clearly show materiality, petition must be accompanied by a 37 CFR 1.102 statement explaining how materiality standard is met. The materiality standard forbids speculation or relying on minor aspects of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Energy Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to (A) discovery/development of energy resources or (B) more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include fossil fuels, hydrogen, nuclear, solar (category A) and reduction of energy consumption (category B). Petition must state basis; no fee required if under 37 CFR 1.102(c). If disclosure not clear, include 37 CFR 1.102 statement explaining materiality; materiality cannot be speculative or based on minor aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Special — Recombinant DNA Safety Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications relating to safety of research in the field of recombinant DNA. Petitions for special status should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining the relationship to safety and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the importance of recombinant DNA research, petitions may be granted for inventions relating to safety; include explanation statements and pay applicable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination — Prerequisites (A)-(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted special (accelerated) status provided applicant complies with: (A) submit petition to make special accompanied by fee; (B) present all claims directed to a single invention, or make an election without traverse as prerequisite; (C) submit a statement that a pre-examination search was made listing field of search by class/subclass, publications, Chemical Abstracts, foreign patents, etc.; (D) submit one copy each of references deemed most closely related if not already of record; (E) submit a detailed discussion of the references, pointing out with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request does not meet all prerequisites, applicant will be notified and given one opportunity to perfect the request via a renewed petition; perfected requests may be granted; no provision for withdrawal from special status once granted; divisional applications must meet requirements on their own; if applicant refuses to elect without traverse, petition denied and application waits its normal turn; follow telephone restriction practice if election needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Defective Special-Status Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where the request for special status does not meet all prerequisites, applicant will be notified of the defects. Applicant will be given one opportunity to perfect the request in a renewed petition. If perfected, the request will be granted; if not perfected in the first renewed petition, further renewed petitions may or may not be considered at the discretion of the Technology Center Special Program Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants get one chance to correct defects; Technology Center discretion applies thereafter; if the petition is defective and not corrected, application remains in regular queue.
